De-identification and disclosure control

Source: vignettes/deidentification.Rmd
deidentification.Rmd
library(vaxsurvR)

The salt

Deterministic hashing lets you link a child across survey rounds without carrying their name. It only works as protection if the hash is salted with a secret: the space of plausible child identifiers is small enough that an unsalted hash can be reversed by enumeration in seconds.

vaxsurvR therefore ships no default salt, and refuses to hash without one.

hash_identifier("CH0001")
#> Error in `vcs_abort()`:
#> ! `salt` is required. Read it from an environment variable, e.g. `Sys.getenv("VAXSURVR_SALT")`; never hard-code it.

In production the salt comes from the environment and never appears in a script:

salt <- Sys.getenv("VAXSURVR_SALT")

For this vignette we use an obvious placeholder:

salt <- "vignette-salt-not-for-production"

The salt is used and discarded. It is never written to the output data, the de-identification record, the object metadata, the cleaning log, or the console.

Finding what needs treating

identify_pii() scans column names and values, and reports what the dictionary names outright.

pii <- identify_pii(vcs_example_raw, vcs_example_dictionary)
pii
#> # A tibble: 48 × 5
#>    variable       category  basis                        confidence n_nonmissing
#>    <chr>          <chr>     <chr>                        <chr>             <int>
#>  1 address        address   "dictionary concept \"addre… certain             600
#>  2 CG_NAME_1_1    name      "dictionary concept \"careg… certain             214
#>  3 CG_NAME_1_2    name      "dictionary concept \"careg… certain              42
#>  4 CG_NAME_2_1    name      "dictionary concept \"careg… certain               0
#>  5 CG_NAME_2_2    name      "dictionary concept \"careg… certain               0
#>  6 CVH01_date_1_1 telephone "values look like phone num… likely              116
#>  7 CVH01_date_1_2 telephone "values look like phone num… likely               15
#>  8 CVH02_date_1_1 telephone "values look like phone num… likely               85
#>  9 CVH02_date_1_2 telephone "values look like phone num… likely               10
#> 10 CVH03_date_1_1 telephone "values look like phone num… likely               67
#> # ℹ 38 more rows

confidence == "certain" means the dictionary said so. "likely" means a pattern matched. Neither is a substitute for reading the free-text fields: a caregiver name written into an observation box is invisible to any automated scan.

Hashing 

hash_identifier(c("CH0001", "CH0002"), salt = salt)
#> [1] "ABFE660E28E9" "C40EC41A988F"

Deterministic given the salt:

identical(
  hash_identifier("CH0001", salt = salt),
  hash_identifier("CH0001", salt = salt)
)
#> [1] TRUE

A namespace separates uses of the same identifier, so a child identifier hashed for the coverage file and for the serology file cannot be cross-walked by someone holding only one of them:

hash_identifier("CH0001", salt = salt, namespace = "coverage")
#> [1] "2D6D0C095EDB"
hash_identifier("CH0001", salt = salt, namespace = "serology")
#> [1] "881FABFFB37D"

Geography

GPS coordinates are the highest-risk variable in a household survey: a coordinate pair plus an administrative unit identifies a dwelling.

names(vcs_example$households)
#>  [1] "interview_id"   "household_id"   "psu"            "segment"       
#>  [5] "stratum"        "province"       "district"       "health_zone"   
#>  [9] "health_area"    "residence"      "interview_date" "duration_min"  
#> [13] "enumerator"     "team"           "supervisor"     "gps_lat"       
#> [17] "gps_lon"        "gps_accuracy"   "eligible"       "consent"       
#> [21] "n_eligible"     "telephone"      "address"

Drop coordinates outright:

d1 <- generalize_geography(vcs_example)
setdiff(names(vcs_example$households), names(d1$households))
#> [1] "gps_lat"      "gps_lon"      "gps_accuracy"

Or coarsen them, if within-cluster geometry matters to the analysis. Two decimal places is roughly a kilometre:

d2 <- generalize_geography(vcs_example, round_gps = 2)
head(d2$households$gps_lat, 3)
#> [1] -5.89 -5.88 -5.89

Truncate the administrative hierarchy, and suppress small cells:

d3 <- generalize_geography(vcs_example, lowest_level = "district", min_cell = 10)
intersect(c("province", "district", "health_zone", "health_area"),
          names(d3$households))
#> [1] "province" "district"

Age

An exact date of birth is a quasi-identifier. Banding replaces it:

d4 <- generalize_age(vcs_example, breaks = c(0, 12, 18, 24, Inf))
table(d4$children$age_band, useNA = "ifany")
#> 
#>   [0,12)  [12,18)  [18,24) [24,Inf] 
#>        0      125      129        2
"child_dob" %in% names(d4$children)
#> [1] FALSE

Date shifting

Shifting every date belonging to one household by the same offset preserves the intervals between doses – the analytically useful quantity – while the calendar dates are no longer real.

shifted <- shift_dates(vcs_example, salt = salt, max_days = 30)

a <- vcs_example$vaccinations
b <- shifted$vaccinations
cid <- a$child_id[!is.na(a$card_date)][1]

data.frame(
  original = a$card_date[a$child_id == cid],
  shifted  = b$card_date[b$child_id == cid]
)
#>      original    shifted
#> 1  2025-02-05 2025-02-13
#> 2        <NA>       <NA>
#> 3  2025-03-27 2025-04-04
#> 4  2025-03-17 2025-03-25
#> 5  2025-03-23 2025-03-31
#> 6  2025-04-25 2025-05-03
#> 7  2025-04-16 2025-04-24
#> 8        <NA>       <NA>
#> 9  2025-06-06 2025-06-14
#> 10 2025-05-21 2025-05-29
#> 11       <NA>       <NA>
#> 12       <NA>       <NA>
#> 13       <NA>       <NA>
#> 14 2025-11-02 2025-11-10

Intervals are identical:

identical(
  diff(a$card_date[a$child_id == cid]),
  diff(b$card_date[b$child_id == cid])
)
#> [1] TRUE

The offsets are derived from the salt, so a team holding the salt can reproduce the shift and nobody else can recover it.

The whole pipeline 

anon <- deidentify_vcs(
  vcs_example,
  remove     = c("child_name", "caregiver_name", "telephone", "address"),
  hash       = c("child_id", "household_id"),
  salt       = salt,
  age_bands  = c(0, 12, 18, 24, Inf),
  geography  = list(lowest_level = "health_zone", round_gps = 2)
)
anon$deidentification$actions
#> [1] "removed direct identifiers: child_name, caregiver_name, telephone, address"
#> [2] "hashed identifiers (salted SHA-256): child_id, household_id"               
#> [3] "banded age at 0/12/18/24/Inf months"                                       
#> [4] "coarsened geography"

The salt is absent from the record of what was done:

anon$deidentification$salt
#> NULL
anon$deidentification$salt_used
#> [1] TRUE

The dataset still analyses. Hashing preserves the child-vaccination link:

head(anon$children$child_id, 3)
#> [1] "B510585B28A0" "77804D0E8050" "DDCB9A221D70"
all(anon$vaccinations$child_id %in% anon$children$child_id)
#> [1] TRUE
estimate_coverage(vcs_design(derive_vaccination_status(anon)),
                  vaccines = c("BCG", "PENTA3"))
#> <vcs_estimate: 2 row(s)>
#>   evidence : card_or_recall
#> # A tibble: 2 × 13
#>   indicator domain    numerator denominator estimate     se conf_low conf_high
#>   <chr>     <chr>         <dbl>       <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 BCG       <overall>       218         253    0.852 0.0235    0.806     0.898
#> 2 PENTA3    <overall>       137         255    0.543 0.0302    0.484     0.602
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: n_unweighted <dbl>, deff <dbl>, neff <dbl>, icc <dbl>,
#> #   ci_method <chr>

Measuring what is left

k-anonymity asks, for each record, how many other records share its combination of quasi-identifiers. Records in small groups are the ones that could be singled out by someone with background knowledge.

assess_reidentification_risk(vcs_example)
#> <vcs_risk: k-anonymity screening>
#>   quasi-identifiers: province, district, health_zone, health_area, residence, stratum, sex
#>   records          : 256
#>   minimum k        : 1
#>   median k         : 5
#>   unique records   : 6 (2.3%)
#>   below k = 5      : 90 (35.2%)
#>   Consider generalize_geography() or generalize_age() before release.

Coarsening geography raises k:

assess_reidentification_risk(
  generalize_geography(vcs_example, lowest_level = "province")
)
#> <vcs_risk: k-anonymity screening>
#>   quasi-identifiers: province, residence, stratum, sex
#>   records          : 256
#>   minimum k        : 20
#>   median k         : 33
#>   unique records   : 0 (0.0%)
#>   below k = 5      : 0 (0.0%)

This is a screening tool. It measures only what the chosen quasi-identifiers capture, and it says nothing at all about identifiers hiding in free text. Read those fields before release.

Before a file leaves the team

  • drop_raw = TRUE (the default) removes the preserved raw import, which still contains every identifier.
  • Export the cleaning log with exclude_variables set for anything sensitive.
  • Re-run identify_pii() on the file you are about to send, not on the one you started from.
  • Keep the salt, the identifier crosswalk and the GPS offsets in a restricted location, separate from the shareable file.
